analysis: The PR changes only docs/threat-model.yaml, adding an 8-line header comment at head lines 41-48. It records an SDK 27.2 Date-comparison availability review. App Attest key-generation budget, enrollment resume, stall restart and key history checks use timeIntervalSince(_:) in place of >= / <=. SDK 27.2 back-deploys those two operators as weak imports that pre-release macOS 27.2 lacks, which crashed the provider in a loop. The comment states that thresholds and results are unchanged, and that release builds refuse binaries importing either symbol via scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py. Both supplied units are base-side excerpts of the surrounding file (TB-013 and threats T-007 to T-043, including T-041 prefix cache). Neither contains the changed lines, which come only from the patch excerpt. The excerpts show no threat, mitigation or status edits, so I found no weakened control, new attack surface or invalidated assumption. The documented change is availability-hardening and the threat model's own claim that it does not revalidate older entries is reasonable. Unverified: the supplied evidence has no source for the Swift Date-comparison changes or for the weak-import check script. I could not confirm that the described behavior is implemented, that timeIntervalSince substitution preserves boundary semantics, or that the release gate runs. The comment is also a claim only. Integration should check the code diff if one exists, particularly App Attest budget and expiry boundary comparisons (A-015, A-016, T-053, T-057). No findings are warranted from the docs-only evidence.
